outcome: Antepartum haemorrhage due to Abruptio placentae
cohort: The study cohort consisted of 286 patients diagnosed with severe preeclampsia, predominantly primigravida, unbooked, from rural backgrounds, and aged 20-30 years.
finding: The study found a high incidence of both maternal (e.g., PPH, eclampsia, maternal death) and perinatal complications (e.g., prematurity, low birth weight, NICU admission, perinatal mortality) in patients with severe preeclampsia.
mod_finding: The study found that vaginal delivery was the common mode of delivery (56.29%), with 43.70% of patients having a lower segment cesarean section.
